scenario: What is cloud computing?

options.text: Computing services delivered over the internet
Servers bought and run in your own building
Files stored only on portable USB drives
Software installed only on one laptop

explanation: Cloud computing is the delivery of computing services (servers, storage, databases, networking, software, analytics) over the internet. You rent capacity from a provider instead of buying and running it yourself, and you typically pay only for what you use. Owning servers in your own building is the on-premises model, not the cloud.

refs.title: Describe cloud computing: What is cloud computing

scenario: Under the shared responsibility model, which is ALWAYS the customer's responsibility, no matter the service type?
explanation: Responsibility for information and data, devices, and accounts and identities stays with the customer in every deployment type (on-premises, IaaS, PaaS, SaaS). Microsoft is always responsible for the physical datacenter, physical network and physical hosts. Everything in between shifts as you move from IaaS toward SaaS.

refs.title: Describe cloud computing: Describe the shared responsibility model
Shared responsibility in the cloud - Microsoft Azure

scenario: A company runs virtual machines in Azure (IaaS). Who is responsible for patching the VM's operating system?

options.note: Microsoft manages the hardware, not the guest OS in IaaS.

explanation: With IaaS you rent the virtual machine, so you manage the guest operating system, including patching, plus the apps and data on it. Microsoft only manages the underlying host, network and datacenter. Patching moves to Microsoft only when you choose PaaS or SaaS.

refs.title: Describe cloud computing: Describe the shared responsibility model
Describe cloud service types: Describe Infrastructure as a Service

scenario: Which cloud model uses only infrastructure owned and used by a single organization?
explanation: A private cloud is infrastructure used by a single organization. It can sit in the organization's own datacenter or be hosted by a provider, but it isn't shared with other tenants. A public cloud is owned by a provider and shared across customers, and a hybrid cloud combines the two.

refs.title: Describe cloud computing: Define cloud models

scenario: A company keeps sensitive databases in its own datacenter but runs its website in Azure, connected together. Which cloud model is this?

options.note: Part of it is on premises.
Part of it is in Azure.
Shared by a group of organizations.

explanation: A hybrid cloud combines a private cloud or on-premises datacenter with a public cloud, with the two connected so data and apps can move between them. Here the sensitive databases stay on premises and the website runs in Azure. Public-only or private-only would mean everything lives in just one place.

refs.title: Describe cloud computing: Define cloud models

scenario: A startup wants no upfront hardware costs and to pay only for the resources it uses. Which model describes this?
explanation: The consumption-based model means no upfront infrastructure purchase: you pay only for the resources you use, when you use them. That is exactly what the startup wants. A capital expenditure model is the opposite, with a large upfront spend on hardware.

refs.title: Describe cloud computing: Describe the consumption-based model

scenario: Buying physical servers for an on-premises datacenter is an example of what type of spending?
explanation: Capital expenditure (CapEx) is upfront spending on physical assets such as servers and datacenter space, whose value is recovered over time. Operational expenditure (OpEx) is spending on services as you use them, and that is how cloud billing normally works.

refs.title: Describe cloud computing: Describe the consumption-based model

scenario: What does "serverless" mean in cloud computing?

options.text: The provider manages servers; you just run code
The app runs with no servers anywhere
options.note: Servers still exist; you don't manage them.

options.text: You must buy and rack your own servers
Apps can only run on your own laptop

explanation: Serverless doesn't mean there are no servers. It means the provider manages them, so you only supply code and are billed for what executes. Azure Functions is the classic example. The 'no servers anywhere' option is the common misreading of the name.

refs.title: Describe Azure compute services: Describe Azure functions
Azure Functions Scale and Hosting

scenario: An online store automatically adds more servers during a holiday sale and removes them afterward. Which cloud benefit is this?
explanation: Elasticity is the ability to add resources automatically when demand rises and remove them when it falls, like the holiday sale scaling out and back in. Predictability is about forecasting cost and performance, governance is about standards and compliance, and manageability is about tooling.

refs.title: Describe the benefits of using cloud services: Describe the benefits of high availability and scalability in the cloud

scenario: What is the difference between vertical and horizontal scaling?

options.text: Vertical adds power to a VM; horizontal adds more VMs
Vertical adds more VMs; horizontal adds power
Both mean moving to another region

explanation: Vertical scaling (scale up) makes a single VM more powerful by adding CPU or RAM. Horizontal scaling (scale out) adds more VM instances and spreads the load across them. They aren't the same thing, and neither involves moving to another region.

refs.title: Describe the benefits of using cloud services: Describe the benefits of high availability and scalability in the cloud

scenario: What does high availability in the cloud mean?

options.text: Services stay running with minimal downtime
Services run in one datacenter only

explanation: High availability means a service keeps running with minimal downtime, even when components fail. Azure expresses this as an SLA, a guaranteed uptime percentage such as 99.9% or 99.99%. It isn't about price, and running in one datacenter makes availability worse, not better.

refs.title: Describe the benefits of using cloud services: Describe the benefits of high availability and scalability in the cloud

scenario: What is a service-level agreement (SLA) in Azure?

options.text: Microsoft's uptime commitment for a service
A contract that fixes the price of each VM
A list of features planned for next year
A security certificate for Azure websites

explanation: An SLA is Microsoft's commitment on a service's uptime and connectivity, expressed as a percentage. If Microsoft misses it, you can claim service credits. It is not a price contract, a roadmap or a certificate.

refs.title: Describe Azure compute services: Describe Azure virtual machines
Describe the benefits of using cloud services: Describe the benefits of high availability and scalability in the cloud

scenario: A company wants to be able to forecast its cloud costs and performance. Which cloud benefit is this?
explanation: Predictability covers both performance (autoscaling and load balancing keep the experience consistent) and cost (forecasting and cost-management tools let you plan spend). Elasticity is about scaling with demand, and agility is about how quickly you can deploy.

refs.title: Describe the benefits of using cloud services: Describe the benefits of reliability and predictability in the cloud

scenario: Which cloud benefit lets a company apply templates and policies so all deployments meet company standards?
explanation: Governance in the cloud means using templates, policies and compliance tooling so every deployment meets corporate standards. In Azure that's the role of services like Azure Policy. Elasticity, latency and reliability aren't about enforcing standards.

refs.title: Describe the benefits of using cloud services: Describe the benefits of security and governance in the cloud

scenario: What does reliability mean in cloud computing?

options.text: Recovering from failures and continuing to work
Running workloads in just one region

explanation: Reliability is the ability of a system to recover from failures and keep working. Designing across multiple regions and zones is the usual approach. Cutting cost or restyling the portal isn't reliability, and running in a single region makes a workload less reliable.

refs.title: Describe the benefits of using cloud services: Describe the benefits of reliability and predictability in the cloud

scenario: Which describes managing cloud resources through the portal, CLI, APIs or automation?

options.note: Also a benefit, but this describes how you manage it.

explanation: Manageability has two sides. Management of the cloud is the automation of the platform itself (autoscale, templates, monitoring). Management in the cloud is how you operate it, through the portal, CLI, APIs or PowerShell. The question describes the tools you use, which is the wording the exam keys on.

refs.title: Describe the benefits of using cloud services: Describe the benefits of manageability in the cloud

scenario: Which cloud service type gives the customer the most control over the operating system?
explanation: IaaS gives the customer the most control, because you manage the operating system, runtime, apps and data on a virtual machine. PaaS hands the OS to the provider, and SaaS hands almost everything over. 'Function as a service' is serverless, where you don't see the OS at all.

refs.title: Describe cloud service types: Describe Infrastructure as a Service

scenario: A team wants to deploy a web app without managing servers or operating systems, but still write its own code. Which service type fits?

options.note: You can't deploy your own code.

explanation: PaaS lets developers deploy and run their own code without managing servers or operating systems. Azure App Service is the standard example. IaaS would still leave OS management with the team, and SaaS gives a finished application with no custom code.

refs.title: Describe cloud service types: Describe Platform as a Service
Overview of Azure App Service

scenario: A company uses Microsoft 365 for email and documents. Which service type is this?

options.note: You don't build apps on it.
A deployment model, not a service type.

explanation: SaaS delivers a complete, ready-to-use application. Microsoft 365 email and documents are the textbook example, where the customer only manages users, data and settings. PaaS and IaaS both require you to build or install the application yourself.

refs.title: Describe cloud service types: Describe Software as a Service

scenario: A company is moving existing servers to the cloud with as few changes as possible (lift and shift). Which service type fits best?

options.note: Replaces the app instead of moving it.

explanation: Lift and shift means moving existing servers to the cloud with minimal change, and IaaS virtual machines are the closest match to on-premises servers. PaaS and serverless usually require changes to the application, and SaaS replaces it entirely.

refs.title: Describe cloud service types: Describe Infrastructure as a Service

scenario: Which is an advantage of the public cloud?

options.text: No upfront hardware purchase is required

options.note: Public cloud is multi-tenant by default.

explanation: A public cloud has no upfront hardware purchase: you provision resources in minutes and pay as you go. Full control of the physical hardware and single-tenant hardware by default describe a private cloud, and public cloud can't work without internet connectivity.

refs.title: Describe cloud computing: Define cloud models

scenario: What is a key benefit of a private cloud?

options.text: No upfront hardware costs at all
options.note: Private clouds usually need hardware investment.

explanation: A private cloud gives the organization complete control over its resources, which suits strict compliance requirements. The trade-off is that you pay for the hardware and maintain it. Upfront-free, unlimited on-demand capacity and no maintenance are public cloud benefits.

refs.title: Describe cloud computing: Define cloud models

scenario: Which pricing option gives the biggest discount for a VM that will run continuously for three years?

options.note: Can be evicted at any time.

explanation: Azure Reservations give a significant discount, up to roughly 72% versus pay-as-you-go, when you commit to a resource for one or three years. For a VM that runs continuously for three years, the three-year reservation saves the most. Spot VMs are cheap but can be evicted, so they don't suit an always-on workload.

refs.title: What are Azure Reservations?
Describe cost management in Azure: Describe cost optimization options in Azure

scenario: A batch job can be interrupted and restarted at any time. Which VM pricing option is cheapest?
explanation: Spot VMs use Azure's spare capacity at deep discounts but can be evicted when Azure needs the capacity back. That makes them ideal for interruptible work such as a restartable batch job. Reserved instances and Dedicated Hosts are for steady, always-on workloads.

refs.title: About Azure Spot Virtual Machines
Describe cost management in Azure: Describe cost optimization options in Azure

scenario: A company has existing Windows Server licenses with Software Assurance. How can it save on Azure VMs?

options.text: Use a larger VM size with more memory

explanation: Azure Hybrid Benefit lets you apply existing Windows Server and SQL Server licenses that have Software Assurance (or qualifying subscriptions) to Azure, so you pay only the base compute rate. Spot pricing and larger VM sizes don't reuse existing licenses.

refs.title: Azure Hybrid Benefit
Describe cost management in Azure: Describe cost optimization options in Azure

scenario: Which describes the benefit of geo-distribution in Azure?

options.text: Running apps close to users worldwide
Keeping all data in a single building
Removing the need for any backups

explanation: Geo-distribution means running apps close to users in regions worldwide, which cuts latency and also supports disaster recovery. It isn't about keeping everything in one building or removing the need for backups.

refs.title: Describe the benefits of using cloud services: Describe the benefits of high availability and scalability in the cloud
What are Azure regions?

scenario: Which is an example of a serverless Azure service?
explanation: Azure Functions is serverless: your code runs in response to events, Azure manages the infrastructure, and on the Consumption plan you're billed per execution. Virtual Machines, Dedicated Host and Azure VMware Solution all require you to manage infrastructure.

refs.title: Describe Azure compute services: Describe Azure functions
Azure Functions Overview

scenario: What does "agility" mean as a cloud benefit?

options.text: Running only in one fixed region

explanation: Agility is the ability to deploy and configure resources quickly, in minutes instead of waiting on hardware purchase cycles. That lets teams experiment and react to change fast. Being fixed to a region or locked from change is the opposite.

refs.title: Describe the benefits of using cloud services: Describe the benefits of manageability in the cloud
Describe the benefits of using cloud services: Describe the benefits of high availability and scalability in the cloud

scenario: Which security responsibility moves to Microsoft when a company switches from IaaS to PaaS?
explanation: Moving from IaaS to PaaS shifts operating system and runtime patching to Microsoft. The customer still owns identities, data classification and devices in every model. That's why patching is the one item here that changes hands.

refs.title: Describe cloud computing: Describe the shared responsibility model
Shared responsibility in the cloud - Microsoft Azure

scenario: What is multicloud?

options.text: Using more than one cloud provider
Using several regions of one provider
Running several VMs on one physical host
Using both IaaS and PaaS services together

explanation: Multicloud means using more than one cloud provider, for example Azure plus AWS. Several regions of the same provider is still a single cloud. Azure Arc is Microsoft's tool for managing resources across hybrid and multicloud estates.

refs.title: Describe cloud computing: Define cloud models
Azure Arc overview

scenario: Which statement about the cloud pay-as-you-go model is true?

options.text: You pay for resources while you use them
You pay a fixed amount whatever you use
You must pay for three years upfront

explanation: Pay-as-you-go means you're billed for the resources while you use them, with no upfront commitment. Reservations and savings plans trade a commitment for a lower price. Paying a fixed amount whatever you use, or paying years upfront, describes other models.

refs.title: Describe cloud computing: Describe the consumption-based model

scenario: Which is a benefit of the cloud for security?

options.text: Providers apply patches and protections at scale
Customers never need to secure anything

explanation: A cloud provider applies patches, security updates and physical protections at massive scale, and provides built-in security tools. You still must secure your own identities, data and configuration, so the customer never needing to secure anything is wrong.

refs.title: Describe the benefits of using cloud services: Describe the benefits of security and governance in the cloud

scenario: Which Azure savings option applies a discount across many VM sizes and regions in exchange for a fixed hourly spend commitment?

options.note: Uses spare capacity; not a commitment.

explanation: An Azure savings plan for compute is a flexible hourly spend commitment (1 or 3 years) whose discount applies across many VM sizes, regions and several compute services. Reservations give discounts too, but they're tied to specific resources and regions.

refs.title: What are savings plans?
Describe cost management in Azure: Describe cost optimization options in Azure

scenario: What is an Azure region?

options.text: A single rack of physical servers
A billing account for a company
A group of users in Entra ID

explanation: A region is a geographic area containing one or more datacenters, connected by a dedicated low-latency network. You pick a region when you create most resources. It's not a single rack, a billing construct or an Entra group.

refs.title: Describe the core architectural components of Azure: Describe Azure physical infrastructure
What are Azure regions?

scenario: What is an availability zone?

options.text: A separate datacenter group within a region
A pair of regions in one country
A virtual network in a subscription
A backup copy of a VM

explanation: An availability zone is a physically separate datacenter location inside a region, with its own power, cooling and networking. Regions that support zones have at least three, so an outage in one zone doesn't take down the others.

refs.title: Describe the core architectural components of Azure: Describe Azure physical infrastructure
What are Azure availability zones?

scenario: A VM must stay available if one datacenter in a region fails. What should be used?

options.text: Use a larger VM size with more memory
Add a second managed disk to the VM
Use a static public IP address

explanation: To survive the loss of one datacenter in a region, spread the VMs across availability zones. Because each zone has independent power, cooling and networking, a single failure only affects the VMs in that zone. A bigger VM, extra disk or static IP does nothing for datacenter failure.

refs.title: Describe Azure compute services: Describe Azure virtual machines
What are Azure availability zones?

scenario: What is a region pair?

options.text: Two regions in one geography, paired for recovery
Two availability zones inside one datacenter
Two subscriptions that share one tenant
Two VMs sharing one load balancer

explanation: A region pair is two regions within the same geography, usually hundreds of miles apart. Platform updates roll out to one region of a pair at a time, and Azure prioritizes recovery of one region in each pair after a wide outage. Availability zones are inside a single region, not a pair.

refs.title: Describe the core architectural components of Azure: Describe Azure physical infrastructure
Azure region pairs and nonpaired regions

scenario: Which describes Azure sovereign regions?

options.text: Isolated Azure instances for government or legal needs
Regions with the lowest prices worldwide
Regions reserved for testing new services
Regions that have no availability zones

explanation: Sovereign regions are isolated Azure instances built for specific legal or compliance needs. Azure Government (US) and Microsoft Azure operated by 21Vianet (China) are the examples. They aren't about price or testing.

refs.title: Describe the core architectural components of Azure: Describe Azure physical infrastructure
Azure Government Overview

scenario: What is a resource group?

options.text: A logical container for related resources
A physical rack of servers in a datacenter
A security group of Entra ID users

explanation: A resource group is a logical container for related Azure resources, which you deploy, manage and delete as a unit. It's a management construct, not a physical rack or a security group. Deleting a resource group deletes everything in it.

refs.title: Describe the core architectural components of Azure: Describe Azure management infrastructure
Use the Azure portal and Azure Resource Manager to Manage Resource Groups

scenario: Which statement about resource groups is correct?

options.text: A resource can be in only one resource group at a time
Resource groups can be nested inside each other
A resource can belong to several groups
Deleting a group keeps its resources

explanation: Each resource belongs to exactly one resource group at a time, although you can move it to another group. Resource groups can't be nested, and deleting a group deletes the resources in it.

refs.title: Describe the core architectural components of Azure: Describe Azure management infrastructure
What is Azure Resource Manager?

scenario: What is an Azure subscription used for?

options.text: An address range for a virtual network

explanation: A subscription is a unit of management, billing and scale: it's the boundary for access and for the invoice. Organizations often use separate subscriptions for departments or for environments such as dev and production. It is not a physical location or an IP range.

refs.title: Describe the core architectural components of Azure: Describe Azure management infrastructure
Describe the core architectural components of Azure: Get started with Azure accounts

scenario: Which order shows the Azure hierarchy from top to bottom?

options.text: Management groups, subscriptions, resource groups, resources
Resources, resource groups, subscriptions, management groups
Subscriptions, management groups, resources, resource groups
Resource groups, management groups, resources, subscriptions

explanation: The hierarchy runs management groups, then subscriptions, then resource groups, then resources. Policies and access assigned at a higher level are inherited by everything below it.

refs.title: Describe the core architectural components of Azure: Describe Azure management infrastructure
Organize your resources with management groups - Azure Governance

scenario: A company with 20 subscriptions wants to apply one policy to all of them at once. What should it use?
explanation: A management group sits above subscriptions, so one policy assignment on it is inherited by all 20 subscriptions beneath. A resource group, VNet or storage account only affects what lives inside it.

refs.title: Organize your resources with management groups - Azure Governance
Describe the core architectural components of Azure: Describe Azure management infrastructure

scenario: What is an Azure resource?

options.text: A manageable item, like a VM or database
An Azure region and its datacenters

explanation: A resource is a manageable item available through Azure, such as a VM, storage account, web app or database. Azure Resource Manager creates and manages them. It isn't a contract, a region or a password.

refs.title: Describe the core architectural components of Azure: Describe Azure management infrastructure
What is Azure Resource Manager?

scenario: Which compute option gives full control of the operating system?
explanation: Azure Virtual Machines (IaaS) give full control of the operating system: you choose it, configure it and patch it. Functions, App Service and Container Instances all abstract the OS away.

refs.title: Describe Azure compute services: Describe Azure virtual machines
Overview of virtual machines in Azure

scenario: A company needs many identical VMs that scale automatically with demand. What should it use?
explanation: Virtual Machine Scale Sets create and manage a group of identical, load-balanced VMs and can automatically increase or decrease the number of instances with demand. A single larger VM only scales up, and DNS or Storage Explorer have nothing to do with scaling.

refs.title: Describe Azure compute services: Describe Azure virtual machines
Azure Virtual Machine Scale Sets overview

scenario: What do availability sets protect against?

options.text: The loss of an entire Azure region
Accidental deletion of a VM's data

explanation: Availability sets spread VMs across fault domains (separate racks with their own power and network) and update domains (groups rebooted at different times during maintenance). They protect against a rack failure or planned maintenance, not the loss of a whole region.

refs.title: Describe Azure compute services: Describe Azure virtual machines
Availability sets overview

scenario: Employees need a Windows desktop and apps they can use from any device, hosted in Azure. Which service fits?
explanation: Azure Virtual Desktop delivers virtualized Windows desktops and apps, including multi-session Windows, from Azure to any device. Functions, Blob Storage and DNS aren't desktop services.

refs.title: Describe Azure compute services: Describe Azure virtual desktop
What is Azure Virtual Desktop?

scenario: Which resources are needed for an Azure VM to be created?

options.text: A virtual network, disks and a NIC
A management group and an Azure Policy
An App Service plan and web app
A Log Analytics workspace and agent

explanation: A VM needs a virtual network (with a NIC attached to a subnet) and disks to be created. A public IP and network security group are common but optional extras. Management groups, policies, App Service plans and Log Analytics aren't required.

refs.title: Describe Azure compute services: Describe Azure virtual machines
Overview of virtual machines in Azure

scenario: What is a container?

options.text: A lightweight package of an app and its dependencies
A full virtual machine with its own OS kernel
A storage folder in Blob Storage

explanation: A container is a lightweight, standalone package of an app and its dependencies. It shares the host OS kernel, so it starts quickly and runs the same everywhere. A full VM includes its own OS, which makes it heavier.

refs.title: Describe Azure compute services: Describe Azure containers
Serverless containers in Azure

scenario: Which service runs containers quickly without managing servers or orchestration?
explanation: Azure Container Instances is the simplest way to run a container in Azure with no servers to manage and no orchestration to configure. AKS is for large, orchestrated container estates, so it's more than this scenario needs.

refs.title: Describe Azure compute services: Describe Azure containers
Serverless containers in Azure

scenario: A company needs to orchestrate hundreds of containers with automatic scaling and rolling updates. Which service fits?
explanation: Orchestrating hundreds of containers with automatic scaling and rolling updates is exactly what Azure Kubernetes Service is for. It's a managed Kubernetes service. Container Instances runs individual containers with no orchestration.

refs.title: Describe Azure compute services: Describe Azure containers
What is Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS)?

scenario: Which service hosts web apps and APIs without managing VMs?
explanation: Azure App Service is a PaaS offering for hosting web apps and APIs with built-in scaling and deployment slots, without managing VMs. Virtual Machines would put OS management back on you, and VPN Gateway and Data Box serve other purposes.

refs.title: Describe Azure compute services: Describe application hosting options
Overview of Azure App Service

scenario: Which compute option bills only when code runs in response to events?
explanation: Azure Functions is event-driven and serverless: on the Consumption plan you're billed only when your code runs. Reserved VMs, Dedicated Hosts and scale sets all bill for capacity whether or not it's busy.

refs.title: Describe Azure compute services: Describe Azure functions
Azure Functions Scale and Hosting

scenario: What is an Azure virtual network (VNet)?

options.text: A private network for Azure resources
A physical cable between offices and Azure
A directory of users and groups

explanation: A virtual network (VNet) is a private network in Azure that gives resources isolation, internet communication, connectivity to on-premises networks and traffic filtering. It isn't a website host or a directory.

refs.title: Describe Azure compute services: Describe application hosting options
What is Azure Virtual Network?

scenario: What is a subnet?

options.text: An IP address range within a VNet
A type of storage account for networks

explanation: A subnet is an IP address range within a VNet. Dividing a VNet into subnets lets you organize and secure resources, for example applying different NSG rules to web and database tiers.

refs.title: What is Azure Virtual Network?
Azure Virtual Network Concepts and Best Practices

scenario: Two virtual networks need to communicate privately over the Microsoft backbone. What should be used?

options.text: A public IP on each VM

explanation: Virtual network peering connects two VNets so their resources communicate privately over the Microsoft backbone network, in the same region or across regions (global peering). Public IPs would send traffic over the internet, and DNS or Policy don't connect networks.

refs.title: Azure Virtual Network Peering

scenario: An office needs an encrypted connection over the internet to an Azure virtual network. What should be used?

options.note: Private connection, not over the internet.

explanation: VPN Gateway provides an encrypted tunnel over the public internet to an Azure virtual network, with site-to-site, point-to-site and VNet-to-VNet options. ExpressRoute is private rather than over the internet, so it doesn't match 'over the internet'.

refs.title: About Azure VPN Gateway

scenario: A company needs a private connection to Azure that doesn't go over the public internet. Which service fits?
explanation: ExpressRoute is a dedicated private connection through a connectivity provider that doesn't traverse the public internet, giving more reliability and predictable latency. VPN Gateway tunnels travel over the internet.

refs.title: Azure ExpressRoute Overview: Connect over a private connection

scenario: Which Azure service hosts DNS domains and resolves names using Azure infrastructure?
explanation: Azure DNS hosts your DNS zones and resolves names using Azure's global infrastructure, managed with the same credentials, billing and tools as your other Azure resources. Firewall and Load Balancer don't host DNS domains.

refs.title: Azure DNS Overview: Hosting and Resolution

scenario: What is a private endpoint?

options.text: A private IP for a service, inside your VNet
A public URL for a storage account
A VPN client app for remote workers
A backup copy of a virtual network

explanation: A private endpoint is a network interface with a private IP address from your VNet that connects you privately to a service powered by Azure Private Link. Traffic stays on the private network instead of crossing the public endpoint.

refs.title: What is a private endpoint?

scenario: By default, how can a storage account be reached?

options.text: Through a public endpoint, with authentication
Only from VMs in the same subnet
Only after a private endpoint is created

explanation: By default a storage account is reachable through a public endpoint, and requests must still be authenticated. You can restrict public access with firewall rules or disable it and use private endpoints for private-only access.

refs.title: Firewall rules and network access for Azure Blob, Data Lake, Queue, and Table Storage
Describe Azure storage services: Describe Azure storage accounts

scenario: Which Azure Storage service is best for unstructured data like images and videos?
explanation: Blob Storage is built for massive amounts of unstructured object data such as images, video, documents and backups. Queues hold messages, Tables hold structured NoSQL data, and Disk Storage backs VMs.

refs.title: Describe Azure storage services: Describe Azure storage services
Introduction to Blob (object) Storage

scenario: A team needs a shared network file share that Windows and Linux machines can mount using SMB. Which service fits?
explanation: Azure Files provides fully managed file shares that you mount over SMB (Windows, Linux, macOS) or NFS. Blob, Queue and Table Storage aren't mountable file shares.

refs.title: Describe Azure storage services: Describe Azure storage services
What is Azure Files?

scenario: Which storage service passes messages between application components?
explanation: Queue Storage holds large numbers of messages that application components read asynchronously. It decouples components and buffers work. Files, Disk and Blob Storage don't pass messages.

refs.title: Describe Azure storage services: Describe Azure storage services
Introduction to Azure Queue Storage

scenario: Which storage access tier is cheapest for data that is rarely accessed and can wait hours to be retrieved?

options.note: For data kept 30+ days, accessed infrequently.
For data kept 90+ days with faster access than Archive.

explanation: Archive is the cheapest tier for data that is rarely accessed. It's offline, so the blob must be rehydrated before it can be read, which can take hours, and it has a 180-day minimum storage period. Hot, Cool and Cold are online tiers with immediate access.

refs.title: Access tiers for blob data
Describe Azure storage services: Describe Azure storage services

scenario: Data is accessed infrequently and kept for at least 30 days, but must be available immediately. Which tier fits best?

options.note: Higher storage cost for infrequent access.

explanation: Cool is for infrequently accessed data kept for at least 30 days that still needs immediate access. It has lower storage cost and higher access cost than Hot. Archive is offline, so it fails the 'available immediately' requirement.

refs.title: Access tiers for blob data

scenario: Which redundancy option keeps three copies of data in a single datacenter?
explanation: LRS stores three copies of your data within a single datacenter in the primary region. It's the cheapest redundancy option and protects against drive and rack failures, but not against the loss of the datacenter.

refs.title: Describe Azure storage services: Describe Azure storage redundancy
Data redundancy

scenario: Data must survive the loss of an entire region. Which redundancy option fits?
explanation: GRS copies data synchronously three times in the primary region (LRS), then asynchronously to a secondary region hundreds of miles away, so data survives the loss of the entire primary region. LRS and ZRS keep data in one region only.

refs.title: Describe Azure storage services: Describe Azure storage redundancy
Data redundancy

scenario: Which redundancy option copies data across three availability zones in one region?

options.note: Read access to a second region.

explanation: ZRS replicates data synchronously across three availability zones in one region, so it stays available if a zone fails. LRS is within one datacenter, and GRS and RA-GRS add a second region.

refs.title: Describe Azure storage services: Describe Azure storage redundancy
Data redundancy

scenario: Which tool copies large amounts of data to or from Azure Storage from the command line?
explanation: AzCopy is a command-line utility for copying blobs and files to, from or between storage accounts, and it's well suited to large transfers. Advisor, Policy and Service Health aren't transfer tools.

refs.title: Describe Azure storage services: Identify Azure file movement options
Copy or move data to Azure Storage by using AzCopy v10

scenario: Which free graphical tool lets users browse and manage storage accounts on their desktop?
explanation: Azure Storage Explorer is a free standalone desktop app for browsing and managing storage accounts on Windows, macOS and Linux. Arc, Migrate and Bastion do other jobs.

refs.title: Describe Azure storage services: Identify Azure file movement options
Get started with Storage Explorer

scenario: A company wants its on-premises Windows file servers to cache files from Azure Files. Which service fits?
explanation: Azure File Sync turns an on-premises Windows Server into a fast local cache of an Azure file share, keeping frequently used files local and tiering the rest to the cloud. AzCopy copies data but doesn't keep a cache in sync, and Data Box is one-time bulk transfer.

refs.title: Describe Azure storage services: Identify Azure file movement options
What is Azure File Sync?

scenario: A company must move 60 TB of data to Azure, but its internet connection is slow. What should it use?
explanation: Azure Data Box is a physical, ruggedized appliance Microsoft ships to you. You copy data to it and ship it back to the Azure datacenter, which beats pushing 60 TB through a slow internet link. AzCopy and Storage Explorer would still depend on that link.

refs.title: Describe Azure storage services: Identify Azure data migration options
Microsoft Azure Data Box overview

scenario: Which service discovers on-premises servers and assesses and migrates them to Azure?
explanation: Azure Migrate is the central hub for discovering on-premises servers, databases and apps, assessing them and migrating them to Azure. Monitor, Advisor and Policy don't perform migration.

refs.title: Describe Azure storage services: Identify Azure data migration options
About Azure Migrate

scenario: What is Microsoft Entra ID?

options.text: A database service for cloud apps
A file sharing service for teams

explanation: Microsoft Entra ID, formerly Azure Active Directory, is Microsoft's cloud-based identity and access management service. It handles sign-in, single sign-on, MFA and access to apps. It isn't a database or file-sharing service.

refs.title: Describe Azure identity, access, and security: Describe Azure directory services
What is Microsoft Entra?

scenario: Legacy apps in Azure need domain join, Group Policy and Kerberos without running domain controllers. Which service fits?

options.text: Microsoft Entra ID with no add-ons
options.note: Doesn't provide traditional domain join or Kerberos for VMs.

explanation: Microsoft Entra Domain Services provides managed domain services (domain join, Group Policy, LDAP, Kerberos/NTLM) compatible with Active Directory, without you deploying or patching domain controllers. Entra ID alone doesn't offer those legacy protocols.

refs.title: Describe Azure identity, access, and security: Describe Azure directory services
Overview of Microsoft Entra Domain Services

scenario: Users sign in once and access many applications without signing in again. What is this?
explanation: Single sign-on lets a user sign in once and access multiple applications without being prompted again. That means fewer passwords to remember and simpler access management. MFA, RBAC and Conditional Access address other problems.

refs.title: Describe Azure identity, access, and security: Describe Azure authentication methods
What is single sign-on in Microsoft Entra ID?

scenario: Which is an example of multifactor authentication (MFA)?

options.text: A password plus a phone app code
A password typed in twice to confirm
A very long, complex password only
A username and a strong password

explanation: MFA requires two or more kinds of proof: something you know (a password), something you have (a phone or security key) and something you are (a fingerprint or face). A password plus an authenticator app code is two different factors. Two passwords, or one long password, is still one factor.

refs.title: Describe Azure identity, access, and security: Describe Azure authentication methods
Microsoft Entra multifactor authentication overview

scenario: Which authentication method lets users sign in without a password, such as with Windows Hello or a FIDO2 key?
explanation: Passwordless authentication removes the password entirely, using something like Windows Hello for Business, the Microsoft Authenticator app or a FIDO2 security key. It's more secure than passwords because there's nothing to phish or reuse.

refs.title: Describe Azure identity, access, and security: Describe Azure authentication methods
Passkeys (FIDO2) authentication method in Microsoft Entra ID

scenario: A company wants partner users to sign in to its apps with their own credentials. Which feature fits?
explanation: External identities (Microsoft Entra External ID) let people outside your organization, such as partners, sign in to your apps with their own credentials. DNS, locks and Advisor have no role in identity.

refs.title: Describe Azure identity, access, and security: Describe Azure external identities
Microsoft Entra External ID Overview

scenario: A company wants MFA only when users sign in from outside the office network. Which feature fits?
explanation: Conditional Access evaluates signals such as location, device, user and risk, then enforces requirements such as MFA. 'MFA only outside the office network' is a location-based Conditional Access policy. Azure Policy and locks govern resources, not sign-ins.

refs.title: Describe Azure identity, access, and security: Describe Azure conditional access
Microsoft Entra Conditional Access: Zero Trust Policy Engine

scenario: A user should be able to view resources in a resource group but not change them. What should be assigned?

options.text: The Owner role on the group
The Contributor role on the group
A delete lock on the group

explanation: Reader lets a user view resources but not change them. Azure RBAC assigns roles at management group, subscription, resource group or resource scope, so assign Reader on that resource group. Owner and Contributor can modify resources, and a delete lock isn't a role.

refs.title: Describe Azure identity, access, and security: Describe Azure role-based access control
Azure built-in roles for General - Azure RBAC: Reader

scenario: What is the principle of Zero Trust?

options.text: Never trust, always verify every request
Trust everything inside the corporate network

explanation: Zero Trust means never trust, always verify. Its principles are to verify explicitly, use least-privilege access, and assume breach. Trusting everything inside the corporate network is the old perimeter model that Zero Trust replaces.

refs.title: Describe Azure identity, access, and security: Describe Zero Trust model

scenario: What is defense in depth?

options.text: Multiple layers of security protecting data
A single strong firewall at the edge

explanation: Defense in depth uses multiple layers of protection so that if one fails, others still protect your data. The layers are physical security, identity and access, perimeter, network, compute, application and data. A single strong firewall is just one layer.

refs.title: Describe Azure identity, access, and security: Describe defense-in-depth

scenario: Which service assesses security posture and protects workloads across Azure, on-premises and other clouds?
explanation: Microsoft Defender for Cloud assesses your security posture with a secure score and recommendations, and provides threat protection for workloads in Azure, on-premises and other clouds. Cost Management, DNS and Migrate aren't security tools.

refs.title: Describe Azure identity, access, and security: Describe Microsoft Defender for Cloud
Microsoft Defender for Cloud overview

scenario: Which factor can increase Azure costs?

options.note: Inbound data transfer is generally free.

explanation: Data leaving Azure (egress) is billed, while data coming in is typically free. Other cost factors include resource type, usage, region, bandwidth and reservations. Empty resource groups and tags carry no charge.

refs.title: Describe cost management in Azure: Describe factors that can affect costs in Azure
Plan to manage Azure costs

scenario: Why might the same VM cost more in one region than another?

options.text: Costs depend on the user's time zone

explanation: Azure prices vary by region because of local infrastructure costs, taxes and demand, so the same VM can cost more in one location than another. Time zone and resource groups don't affect price.

refs.title: Describe cost management in Azure: Describe factors that can affect costs in Azure

scenario: A company wants to estimate the monthly cost of a new Azure solution before deploying it. Which tool should it use?
explanation: The Azure pricing calculator estimates the monthly cost of specific services and configurations before you deploy anything. Monitor, Policy and Service Health don't estimate cost.

refs.title: Describe cost management in Azure: Explore the pricing calculator

scenario: Which tool shows current spending, forecasts and budgets with alerts for an Azure subscription?
explanation: Microsoft Cost Management analyzes current spending, shows forecasts and lets you set budgets that alert you at thresholds. DNS, Arc and Bastion aren't cost tools.

refs.title: Describe cost management in Azure: Describe the Microsoft Cost Management tool
Optimize your cloud investment with Cost Management

scenario: Finance wants an email when a department's Azure spending reaches 80% of its monthly amount. What should be set up?

options.note: Policy controls resource settings, not spending alerts.
Tags help group costs but don't send alerts.

explanation: A budget with an alert in Cost Management sends an email when actual or forecasted spend reaches a threshold, such as 80%. Budgets notify but don't stop resources by themselves. Locks and tags don't send spending alerts, and Azure Policy has no spending rule.

refs.title: Tutorial - Create and manage budgets
Describe cost management in Azure: Describe the Microsoft Cost Management tool

scenario: What are tags used for in Azure?
explanation: Tags are name-value pairs of metadata, such as Department=Finance, that you attach to resources and resource groups. They help with organization, cost reporting and automation. Tags don't encrypt, connect or authenticate anything.

refs.title: Describe cost management in Azure: Describe the purpose of tags
Use tags to organize your Azure resources and management hierarchy

scenario: Finance needs costs broken down by department across several resource groups. What should be applied to resources?
explanation: A Department tag applied to each resource lets Cost Management group and filter costs by department, even across several resource groups. Locks, zones and region pairs don't categorize costs.

refs.title: Describe cost management in Azure: Describe the purpose of tags
Use tags to organize your Azure resources and management hierarchy

scenario: A company must ensure resources are only created in approved regions. Which service enforces this?

options.note: Controls who can act, not what settings are allowed.

explanation: Azure Policy evaluates resources against rules, such as an allowed-locations policy, and can deny noncompliant deployments. RBAC controls who can act, Advisor only recommends, and Monitor only observes.

refs.title: Describe features and tools in Azure for governance and compliance: Describe the purpose of Azure Policy
Overview of Azure Policy

scenario: What is the difference between Azure Policy and Azure RBAC?

options.text: Policy controls resource settings; RBAC controls user permissions
Policy controls user permissions; RBAC controls settings

explanation: RBAC decides who can do what (user permissions), while Azure Policy decides what resources and configurations are allowed (resource settings). A user with the Owner role can still be blocked by a policy that denies a non-compliant setting.

refs.title: Describe features and tools in Azure for governance and compliance: Describe the purpose of Azure Policy
Overview of Azure Policy: Azure Policy and Azure RBAC

scenario: Which resource lock prevents a resource from being deleted but still allows changes?
explanation: A CanNotDelete lock (shown as Delete in the portal) lets authorized users read and modify a resource but blocks deletion. A ReadOnly lock also blocks changes. Locks apply to everyone, including Owners.

refs.title: Describe features and tools in Azure for governance and compliance: Describe the purpose of resource locks
Lock your Azure resources to protect your infrastructure

scenario: A production database must not be changed or deleted by anyone, even administrators, without first removing a safeguard. What should be applied?
explanation: A ReadOnly lock stops both changes and deletion, and it applies even to administrators until someone with the right permission removes the lock. Tags, budgets and the Reader role don't prevent changes.

refs.title: Describe features and tools in Azure for governance and compliance: Describe the purpose of resource locks
Lock your Azure resources to protect your infrastructure: Considerations before applying your locks

scenario: Which service helps discover, classify and govern data across on-premises, multicloud and SaaS sources?
explanation: Microsoft Purview provides data governance and risk and compliance solutions: it discovers, classifies and governs data across on-premises, multicloud and SaaS sources. Firewall, Load Balancer and Container Instances don't classify data.

refs.title: Describe features and tools in Azure for governance and compliance: Describe the purpose of Microsoft Purview

scenario: Which statement about Azure Policy is true?

options.text: It audits resources and can block noncompliant ones
It only works on virtual machines
It grants users permissions to resources
It can't be assigned to subscriptions

explanation: Azure Policy audits resources for compliance and, with effects such as deny, can block noncompliant ones. It works on many resource types and can be assigned at management group, subscription or resource group scope. It does not grant permissions; that's RBAC.

refs.title: Describe features and tools in Azure for governance and compliance: Describe the purpose of Azure Policy
Overview of Azure Policy

scenario: Where should a policy be assigned so it applies to every subscription in a company?
explanation: Policy assignments are inherited by child scopes, so assigning at a management group that contains all the subscriptions applies it to every one of them. A resource group, VM or storage account covers only its own contents.

refs.title: Understand scope in Azure Policy
Organize your resources with management groups - Azure Governance

scenario: Which tool provides a web-based graphical interface to manage Azure resources?
explanation: The Azure portal is the web-based graphical interface for building, managing and monitoring resources and creating dashboards. AzCopy, the CLI and ARM templates are command-line or code tools.

refs.title: Describe features and tools for managing and deploying Azure resources: Describe tools for interacting with Azure
What is the Azure portal?

scenario: An admin wants a browser-based shell with Azure CLI and PowerShell ready to use, without installing anything. What should they use?
explanation: Azure Cloud Shell is a browser-based shell, already authenticated with your Azure account, that has Azure CLI and Azure PowerShell ready to use with nothing to install. Storage Explorer and Data Box aren't shells.

refs.title: Describe features and tools for managing and deploying Azure resources: Describe tools for interacting with Azure
What is Azure Cloud Shell?

scenario: Which command-line tools can manage Azure resources from Windows, macOS or Linux?
explanation: Azure CLI (bash-style commands) and Azure PowerShell (cmdlets) both run on Windows, macOS and Linux and manage Azure resources. Batch files, Excel macros and the mobile app are not the cross-platform command-line tools.

refs.title: Describe features and tools for managing and deploying Azure resources: Describe tools for interacting with Azure

scenario: What is Azure Resource Manager (ARM)?

options.text: A tool for copying files to storage
A type of virtual machine image

explanation: Azure Resource Manager is the deployment and management service for Azure. Every request from the portal, CLI, PowerShell, SDKs and REST APIs goes through it, so they all behave consistently.

refs.title: Describe features and tools for managing and deploying Azure resources: Describe Azure Resource Manager and Azure ARM templates
What is Azure Resource Manager?

scenario: A team wants to deploy the same set of resources consistently every time using a JSON file. What should it use?
explanation: ARM templates are JSON files that declaratively describe the resources to deploy, so the same set can be deployed repeatedly and consistently. Advisor, locks and Service Health don't deploy resources.

refs.title: Describe features and tools for managing and deploying Azure resources: Describe Azure Resource Manager and Azure ARM templates
Templates overview

scenario: What is infrastructure as code (IaC)?

options.text: Writing application code inside a VM
Storing source code in Blob Storage

explanation: Infrastructure as code defines infrastructure in code or template files instead of clicking through a portal. That makes deployments repeatable, reviewable and version controlled. It isn't about application code in a VM or encrypting source code.

refs.title: Describe features and tools for managing and deploying Azure resources: Describe Azure Resource Manager and Azure ARM templates
What is Bicep?

scenario: A company wants to manage its on-premises servers and other clouds' Kubernetes clusters from Azure. Which service fits?
explanation: Azure Arc extends Azure management, governance and monitoring to resources outside Azure: on-premises servers and Kubernetes clusters in other clouds. DNS, Data Box and Files don't project external resources into Azure.

refs.title: Describe features and tools for managing and deploying Azure resources: Describe the purpose of Azure Arc
Azure Arc overview

scenario: What is a benefit of using ARM templates over manual portal deployments?
explanation: ARM templates make deployments consistent and repeatable because the same file creates identical environments every time. They don't lower resource prices, bypass permissions or back up data.

refs.title: Describe features and tools for managing and deploying Azure resources: Describe Azure Resource Manager and Azure ARM templates
Templates overview

scenario: Which service gives personalized recommendations to improve cost, security, reliability and performance?
explanation: Azure Advisor analyzes your resource configuration and usage, then gives personalized recommendations across reliability, security, performance, cost and operational excellence. Policy enforces rules, Arc extends management, and Migrate moves workloads.

refs.title: Describe monitoring tools in Azure: Describe the purpose of Azure Advisor
Introduction to Azure Advisor

scenario: A user wants to know whether an Azure outage is affecting their resources. Which service should they check?
explanation: Azure Service Health tells you whether Azure service issues, planned maintenance or health advisories affect the services and regions you use. Advisor gives recommendations and Cost Management shows spend.

refs.title: Describe monitoring tools in Azure: Describe Azure Service Health
What is Azure Service Health?

scenario: Which service collects and analyzes metrics and logs from Azure and on-premises resources?
explanation: Azure Monitor collects, analyzes and acts on metrics and logs from Azure and on-premises resources. DNS, Data Box and Files don't provide telemetry.

refs.title: Describe monitoring tools in Azure: Describe Azure Monitor
Azure Monitor overview

scenario: An admin wants to write queries over collected log data. Which tool should they use?
explanation: Log Analytics is the tool in the Azure portal for writing and running queries against log data collected by Azure Monitor. Queries use Kusto Query Language (KQL). Storage Explorer, AzCopy and the pricing calculator don't query logs.

refs.title: Describe monitoring tools in Azure: Describe Azure Monitor
Overview of Log Analytics in Azure Monitor

scenario: Developers want to monitor a web app's performance, failures and user behavior. Which feature fits?
explanation: Application Insights, a feature of Azure Monitor, provides application performance monitoring: request rates, failures, dependencies and user behavior for a web app. Policy, locks and Data Box don't monitor apps.

refs.title: Describe monitoring tools in Azure: Describe Azure Monitor
Application Insights OpenTelemetry observability overview

scenario: An admin wants to be notified when a VM's CPU stays above 90% for 10 minutes. What should be created?
explanation: An Azure Monitor alert rule can watch a metric such as CPU, and fire when it stays above a threshold for a set time window. It then notifies through an action group. A lock, a budget or a management group doesn't watch performance.

refs.title: Overview of Azure Monitor alerts
Types of Azure Monitor alerts: Metric alerts

scenario: Which part of Service Health shows the health of an individual resource, like a specific VM?
explanation: Resource Health reports the health of an individual resource, such as one specific VM, and helps you tell whether a problem is Azure's or yours. Service Health covers Azure-wide service issues and planned maintenance.

refs.title: Describe monitoring tools in Azure: Describe Azure Service Health
Azure Resource Health overview

scenario: Which Azure tool would recommend resizing or shutting down underused VMs to save money?
explanation: Advisor's cost recommendations identify idle and underused resources, such as VMs with low CPU use, and suggest resizing, shutting down or buying reservations. DNS, Firewall and Purview don't analyze usage for savings.

refs.title: Describe monitoring tools in Azure: Describe the purpose of Azure Advisor
Optimize virtual machine (VM) or virtual machine scale set (VMSS) spend by resizing or shutting down underutilized instances

scenario: What does a service level agreement credit mean for customers?

options.text: A refund when uptime targets are missed
A credit card used for Azure billing

explanation: An SLA credit is a financial remedy: if Microsoft doesn't meet its uptime commitment, you can claim a credit against your bill. It isn't free VMs, a reservation discount or a payment method.

refs.title: Describe the benefits of using cloud services: Describe the benefits of high availability and scalability in the cloud

scenario: How does deploying a VM across availability zones affect its SLA?

options.text: It has no effect on the SLA

explanation: Deploying across availability zones lets a service qualify for a higher SLA, for example 99.99% for VMs in two or more zones, compared with 99.9% for a single VM with premium storage. More redundancy means higher guaranteed uptime.

refs.title: Availability options for Azure Virtual Machines: Availability zones
Describe the benefits of using cloud services: Describe the benefits of high availability and scalability in the cloud

scenario: Which is a correct use of Azure resource tags?

options.text: Identifying the cost center or owner of a resource
Preventing a resource from being deleted

explanation: Tags are metadata such as cost center or owner that help you organize, report on and automate resources. By themselves they don't lock resources, control traffic or grant access.

refs.title: Describe cost management in Azure: Describe the purpose of tags
Use tags to organize your Azure resources and management hierarchy

scenario: Which describes a benefit of using management groups?

options.text: Reducing the price of every VM

explanation: Management groups let you apply governance (policy and RBAC) to many subscriptions at once, and they can be nested to mirror your organization's structure. They don't change prices or replace networking.

refs.title: Organize your resources with management groups - Azure Governance
Describe the core architectural components of Azure: Describe Azure management infrastructure

scenario: A company wants Azure Policy to automatically add a missing tag to new resources. What can the policy do?

options.text: Modify the resource to add the tag

explanation: Azure Policy effects include Audit, Deny, Append, Modify and DeployIfNotExists. The Modify effect can add or update tags on resources as they're created or updated, which is how you add a missing tag automatically. It cannot delete subscriptions or change passwords.

refs.title: Azure Policy definitions modify effect
Azure Policy definitions effect basics

scenario: Which statement about Azure Cost Management is true?

options.text: It can analyze costs by tag, resource group or service
It only works for one VM

explanation: Cost analysis in Cost Management lets you break down and filter costs by tag, resource group, service, location and more, and export the data. It does not delete resources automatically and it works across the whole scope, not one VM.

refs.title: Quickstart - Start using Cost Analysis
Describe cost management in Azure: Describe the Microsoft Cost Management tool

scenario: What is the Azure Monitor agent used for?
explanation: The Azure Monitor agent runs inside a VM (or Arc-enabled server) and sends guest operating system logs and performance data to Azure Monitor. It doesn't copy files, create networks or assign roles.

refs.title: Azure Monitor Agent Overview

scenario: Which is an example of using infrastructure as code with Azure?

options.text: Deploying resources from a Bicep file
Clicking through the portal each time

explanation: Deploying resources from a Bicep file is infrastructure as code: the file defines the infrastructure and Azure builds it from that definition. Bicep compiles to an ARM template for deployment. Clicking through the portal, emailing settings or screenshots is manual configuration.

refs.title: What is Bicep?
Describe features and tools for managing and deploying Azure resources: Describe Azure Resource Manager and Azure ARM templates

scenario: Who can remove a resource lock?

options.text: Users allowed to manage locks, like Owner
Anyone with Reader access to it
No one, because locks are permanent

explanation: A lock can be removed by users who have permission to manage locks, such as Owners and User Access Administrators (Microsoft.Authorization/locks/* actions). Reader access isn't enough, and locks aren't permanent. Remove the lock before changing or deleting the resource.

refs.title: Lock your Azure resources to protect your infrastructure: Who can create or delete locks
Describe features and tools in Azure for governance and compliance: Describe the purpose of resource locks

scenario: A company wants to see whether its resources comply with regulatory standards and its own rules. Which service shows compliance state?
explanation: The Azure Policy compliance dashboard shows which resources are compliant or noncompliant with assigned policies and initiatives, including built-in regulatory compliance initiatives. DNS, Data Box and AzCopy don't evaluate compliance.

refs.title: Get policy compliance data
Describe features and tools in Azure for governance and compliance: Describe the purpose of Azure Policy

scenario: Which describes Azure Monitor alerts' action groups?

options.text: Who to notify and what to run on an alert
A list of resource groups to clean up
A set of VM sizes to scale between
A collection of storage access tiers

explanation: An action group defines who to notify (email, SMS, voice, push) and what to run (such as a Logic App, Azure Function or webhook) when an Azure Monitor alert fires. It's not a cleanup list, a scaling range or a set of access tiers.

refs.title: Create and manage action groups in Azure Monitor
